paragraphs: APOLLO addresses the gap between checking a mathematical proof and generating one correctly. Lean can quickly verify a formal proof, but language models often produce proofs containing mistakes. Repeatedly requesting complete replacements can consume large sampling budgets. APOLLO instead organizes a collaboration that repairs specific failures using feedback from Lean.

The framework starts with a generated proof, then uses agents to inspect it, repair syntax, and identify unsuccessful reasoning steps. It isolates failing sublemmas, applies automated solvers, and asks a language model to handle remaining goals with a small candidate budget. Repaired pieces are assembled and checked again, with repetition bounded by a user-controlled attempt limit.

On miniF2F, APOLLO reports 84.9% accuracy among models below eight billion parameters with fewer than one hundred samples, a category-leading result as of August 2025. It also improves Goedel-Prover-SFT and general-purpose models while reducing sampling requirements. These findings support targeted, compiler-guided repair as an effective way to improve both proof success and generation efficiency.
neurips-2025-apollo-automated-llm-and-le.tldr: APOLLO uses Lean feedback and targeted proof repair to improve automated theorem proving with smaller sampling budgets.

paragraphs: This paper turns a pretrained video diffusion model into a generator designed for real-time interaction. The central requirement is to produce video continuously while accepting controls that influence what comes next. Computationally intensive generation makes that difficult, so the proposed autoregressive adversarial post-training method changes how the pretrained model produces frames.

The resulting model generates one latent frame at a time with a single neural function evaluation. Adversarial training supports an architecture suited to this one-step process. Training also uses student forcing to mitigate the accumulation of errors during successive predictions. The method trains for long-duration generation while making full use of the key-value cache, which retains information used during generation.

The eight-billion-parameter model achieves streaming generation at 24 frames per second and 736 by 416 resolution on one H100. With eight H100s, the reported resolution reaches 1280 by 720 for up to one minute. These results demonstrate the approach's ability to combine sequential generation, interactive control, and real-time output under the stated hardware configurations.
neurips-2025-autoregressive-adversarial-.tldr: Adversarial post-training converts a video diffusion model into a real-time generator that produces one latent frame per neural evaluation.

paragraphs: Federated learning exchanges information between a server and participating clients, creating communication costs in both directions. This paper studies stochastic federated learning, where learning maintains distributions over model parameters. That setting supports uncertainty estimation and offers a structure for incorporating communication costs into the training process itself.

The proposed framework uses remote source generation through Minimal Random Coding. Rather than transmitting an update already sampled at its source, it enables the receiving party to sample from the relevant distribution: the server from local posteriors and clients from the global posterior. Gradually updated prior distributions provide shared side information, connecting communication-aware local optimization with compression of updates.

Simulations report a fivefold to thirty-twofold reduction in total communication while preserving accuracy. The paper also refines bounds on coding costs to quantify trade-offs between uploads and downloads. An extension uses stochastic quantization for conventional federated learning, with a proved contraction property for the biased compressor that supports convergence analysis. Together, these contributions address communication as part of both learning and transmission.
neurips-2025-bi-directional-communicatio.tldr: Remote sampling from parameter distributions reduces communication in both directions of federated learning while preserving accuracy in simulations.

paragraphs: BrainOmni aims to learn a shared representation of EEG and MEG recordings. Both measure neural activity through electromagnetic signals, but their recorded patterns differ, and devices use different sensor configurations. These differences make it difficult to reuse models across recording systems when training is tied to a particular modality or dataset.

The proposed BrainTokenizer converts brain activity across space and time into discrete representations. Its Sensor Encoder explicitly represents sensor layout, orientation, and type, helping accommodate differences between devices and measurement modalities. BrainOmni then uses self-supervised pretraining on these representations to learn unified embeddings. The curated training collection contains 1,997 hours of EEG and 656 hours of MEG from public sources.

Experiments report better performance than existing foundation models and leading task-specific models across several downstream tasks. BrainOmni also generalizes strongly to previously unseen EEG and MEG devices. Joint training on both modalities consistently improves results for each, supporting the value of sharing information across these related measurements while explicitly accounting for how they were recorded.
neurips-2025-brainomni-a-brain-foundatio.tldr: BrainOmni unifies EEG and MEG learning through sensor-aware tokenization and joint pretraining, improving downstream performance and generalization to unseen devices.

paragraphs: DuSA accelerates transformer attention by splitting sparse attention into two complementary stages. Attention must capture nearby relationships as well as dependencies across distant parts of an input. The paper's design gives those roles separate stages, aiming to retain useful information while reducing the computational burden of standard scaled-dot-product attention.

The first stage operates within blocks, gathering local information and incorporating local inductive biases. The second exchanges information between blocks to capture longer-range dependencies. Both stages have low computational complexity and can directly benefit from memory-focused attention acceleration methods. The paper reports that this combination can be faster than some already highly efficient attention mechanisms.

The two-stage design approximates standard attention with less error than basic single-stage sparse mechanisms. Reported task performance can match or exceed standard attention, with low performance loss also observed in some plug-and-play uses. Evaluations span long-range reasoning, image tasks, text-to-video generation, and long-context understanding. The results support applying the same attention design to accelerate both training and inference across models of different sizes.
neurips-2025-dusa-fast-and-accurate-dual.tldr: DuSA combines sparse attention within and between blocks to accelerate transformers while retaining strong performance across diverse tasks.

paragraphs: SpuriVerse examines whether large vision-language models rely on visual shortcuts: incidental features associated with an answer that do not actually justify it. Such associations can break when the input distribution changes. The paper focuses on models pretrained on broad, diverse data, asking whether that breadth protects them against these mistakes.

The authors begin with GPT-4o errors on real-world visual question-answering datasets. They combine model and human annotation with synthetic counterfactual evaluation to identify errors attributable to spurious correlations. The resulting benchmark covers 124 correlation types, each represented by one realistic sample and ten synthetic samples, producing 1,364 multiple-choice questions.

Across fifteen open and closed models, the best reported accuracy is only 35.0%, showing substantial difficulty on this curated challenge. Fine-tuning on synthetic examples emphasizing spurious correlations raises performance to 78.4%. The authors interpret this as evidence suggesting that exposure to diverse shortcut patterns can transfer to unseen situations, with models appearing to consider broader image context. That interpretation remains an empirical suggestion rather than a universal guarantee.
neurips-2025-escaping-the-spuriverse-can.tldr: SpuriVerse exposes persistent visual shortcuts in large vision-language models and suggests targeted synthetic training can improve generalization beyond them.

paragraphs: This paper develops a theoretical account of how attention parameters evolve during training in linearized transformers. It is motivated by empirical observations connecting small initialization scales with improved language-model reasoning. The analysis uses gradient flow, a continuous description of parameter updates, to distinguish two stages that would be obscured by treating training as a single process.

In the first stage, asymmetries introduced by random initialization keep gradients from becoming degenerate. This allows parameter matrices to move systematically away from the small-initialization regime. The matrices then undergo condensation: their directions increasingly align with the target orientation. The emphasis is on how useful directional structure develops from initially small random weights.

In the second stage, key-query matrices that were previously static begin to participate actively in learning. Their involvement drives normalized matrices toward asymptotic rank collapse, meaning their effective directional structure becomes increasingly restricted in the analyzed limit. The resulting two-stage account generalizes classical directional-convergence results. Its conclusions concern the stated linearized training framework; the reasoning observations motivate the analysis rather than constituting its demonstrated outcome.
neurips-2025-from-condensation-to-rank-c.tldr: A gradient-flow analysis of linearized transformers identifies an initial alignment stage followed by asymptotic rank collapse of normalized matrices.

paragraphs: GAMBITTS addresses a distinction that arises when a decision system uses generative AI to deliver an intervention. The system chooses a query, but the user experiences a randomly generated response. Consequently, the chosen action affects the reward through an intermediate treatment whose actual content can be observed after generation.

The method adapts Thompson sampling to model both how treatments are generated and how those treatments produce rewards. This lets learning use information from the intervention that was actually delivered, instead of relying only on the selected query and resulting reward. Language-model-generated messages for mobile health provide the motivating setting for this action-and-treatment separation.

The theoretical analysis separates uncertainty about treatment generation from uncertainty about rewards and derives regret bounds. It identifies conditions under which GAMBITTS has stronger guarantees than standard bandit approaches. In simulations, the method consistently outperforms conventional algorithms by estimating expected rewards more accurately from observed treatments. The contribution is therefore both a formulation of the generative intermediary and a learning method that makes use of it.
neurips-2025-generator-mediated-bandits-.tldr: GAMBITTS improves adaptive decision learning by modeling the generated treatment between a chosen query and its eventual reward.

paragraphs: GUIDED tackles object detection from descriptions that specify both an object and detailed attributes. Existing vision-language representations can mix these components in ways that give attributes too much influence, causing incorrect localization or distorted semantic matching. The paper separates finding the object from deciding which detailed description fits it.

A language model first extracts the coarse object category and descriptive attributes from a class name. The detector uses the subject embedding for localization, keeping that step from being dominated by descriptive details. An attention-based fusion module then selectively introduces useful attribute information into detection queries, preserving distinctions needed for fine-grained recognition.

A final region-level module compares detected regions against complete class descriptions using a refined vision-language model and a projection head that improves alignment. This division assigns localization and attribute discrimination to different pathways while still connecting their information. Experiments on FG-OVD and 3F-OVD report new state-of-the-art results, supporting the benefit of separating these roles when detecting novel categories described by rich text.
neurips-2025-guided-granular-understandi.tldr: GUIDED separates object localization from attribute recognition to improve fine-grained detection of categories described in text.

paragraphs: Graph diffusion models commonly tell the denoiser how much noise has been added to a graph. This paper asks whether that explicit signal is always needed. Its central possibility is that a corrupted graph may already contain enough structural evidence for a model to infer the noise level internally.

The authors build a theoretical framework around Bernoulli edge flips, a corruption process that changes graph connections. They extend the framework to settings where noise affects both graph structure and attributes. This connects the question of conditioning to the information available in the corrupted input, rather than treating an externally supplied noise level as an automatic architectural requirement.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world graph datasets, including GDSS and DiGress models, support the theoretical findings. Models without explicit noise conditioning achieve comparable or better performance while reducing parameters by 4–6% and computation time by 8–10%. The results suggest that high-dimensional graph data often supplies sufficient denoising information. They support simpler architectures in such settings without establishing that conditioning is unnecessary for every graph diffusion problem.
neurips-2025-is-noise-conditioning-neces.tldr: Theory and experiments suggest graph denoisers can often infer noise levels from corrupted graphs, enabling simpler models without explicit noise conditioning.

paragraphs: Dynamic context cutoff aims to stop a language model from processing more input once it has enough information to answer a question. This matters when the relevant evidence occupies only part of a long context. Processing every remaining token can then consume computation without supplying information the task still needs.

The authors identify signals in particular attention heads that predict whether critical information has already been processed. Lightweight classifiers detect these signals and use them to decide when to stop. The stopping decision therefore draws on the model's internal processing of the question and context, rather than relying solely on externally chosen compression rules.

Experiments cover six question-answering datasets, contexts up to 40,000 tokens, and three model families ranging from one to seventy billion parameters. The reported averages combine a 1.33-fold token reduction with a 3.4% accuracy improvement, and the method outperforms other efficiency methods at equivalent reduction rates. The authors also observe a scale-dependent difference: smaller models require probing, while larger models show sufficiency self-assessment through prompting.
neurips-2025-knowing-when-to-stop-effici.tldr: Internal attention signals help language models stop reading once they have sufficient evidence, reducing context processing while improving reported question-answering accuracy.

paragraphs: Model-based Policy Adaptation addresses a gap between evaluating driving predictions in isolation and letting those predictions control a vehicle over time. In closed-loop driving, earlier decisions influence later situations, allowing errors to cascade. The framework adapts pretrained end-to-end driving agents to improve robustness and safety under that feedback.

A geometry-consistent simulator generates diverse counterfactual trajectories, exposing the system to situations beyond its original dataset. These examples train two components: a diffusion-based adapter that refines the base policy's predictions, and a multi-step Q-value model that evaluates longer-term outcomes. During inference, the adapter proposes several trajectories and the value model chooses the candidate with the highest expected utility.

Experiments use nuScenes with a photorealistic closed-loop simulator and report significant improvements across familiar, out-of-domain, and safety-critical scenarios. The authors also examine how counterfactual-data scale and inference-time guidance affect performance. The results support combining simulated alternatives with longer-horizon evaluation to improve deployed policy decisions within the tested simulation setting, where the consequences of actions feed back into subsequent inputs.
neurips-2025-model-based-policy-adaptati.tldr: MPA improves pretrained driving agents in closed-loop simulation by generating candidate trajectories and selecting them using predicted long-term outcomes.

paragraphs: Hierarchical Diffusion Language Models generate language by progressively refining semantic detail. Their vocabulary has multiple levels: detailed tokens map to higher-level tokens with broader meanings. Multiple detailed tokens can therefore share a coarser ancestor, giving the diffusion process an explicit structure for moving between levels of abstraction.

During the forward process, each token is independently replaced by a higher-level ancestor according to a schedule. The reverse process learns to predict the next, more detailed semantic level. This makes generation a changing sequence of refinement tasks, with the model recovering increasingly specific meaning as it proceeds through the hierarchy.

The paper derives closed-form expressions for the diffusion evidence lower bound, providing a mathematical foundation for training. The framework allows flexible implementations and includes the existing MDLM approach as a special case. The authors also derive practical training techniques from their analysis. Text-generation experiments consistently show lower validation and generative perplexity than the evaluated baselines, supporting semantic hierarchies as a useful organizing principle for discrete language diffusion.
neurips-2025-next-semantic-scale-predict.tldr: HDLM generates text by progressively refining coarse semantic tokens into detailed ones, achieving lower perplexity than evaluated baselines.

paragraphs: OCTDiff improves the resolution and visual quality of images from portable optical coherence tomography devices. The goal is particularly relevant to lower-cost imaging, where enhancement could improve diagnostic usefulness. The paper uses an image-to-image diffusion framework tailored to portable OCT and the fine retinal structures these images need to preserve.

Its Adaptive Noise Aggregation module improves denoising dynamics during reverse diffusion. A Multi-Scale Cross-Attention component in the U-Net backbone captures local dependencies across spatial resolutions. The training objective also incorporates clinical quality scores, with the stated aims of reducing overfitting on small clinical datasets and retaining structural details important for retinal diagnosis.

On clinical portable OCT datasets, OCTDiff outperforms convolutional baselines and standard denoising diffusion models, achieving the reported state of the art. These findings support the combined architectural and training choices for the evaluated enhancement task. The authors additionally propose that the method could extend to other medical imaging modalities and improve ophthalmic workflows, presenting those broader applications as potential rather than demonstrated outcomes.
neurips-2025-octdiff-bridged-diffusion-m.tldr: OCTDiff combines specialized diffusion denoising, multiscale attention, and clinically guided training to improve portable OCT image quality.

paragraphs: RANK++LETR addresses a mismatch between a detector's confidence in a proposed line segment and the segment's actual localization quality. Earlier proposal-based methods predict scores and locations together, and those scores may not accurately reflect how good the resulting lines are. The paper makes candidate ranking and refinement explicit learning objectives.

Built on deformable DETR, the model uses its encoder to select line candidates and its decoder to rank and improve them. A line-aware deformable attention module places attention locations within a long, narrow region that aligns with line geometry. This adapts the model's information gathering to the elongated structures it is trying to detect.

The training procedure introduces ranking supervision with contiguous labels determined by detection quality. These labels connect candidate ordering to the quality of the predictions themselves. Experiments report higher prediction accuracy than previous state-of-the-art methods and faster inference than other transformer-based methods. Together, the findings support coordinating geometric refinement with learned ranking so that candidate selection better reflects the quality of detected line segments.
neurips-2025-rank-letr-learn-to-rank-and.tldr: RANK++LETR improves line detection by jointly learning candidate ranking and refinement with attention shaped to line geometry.

paragraphs: RePO investigates how simple the objective for language-model preference learning can be while still producing useful alignment. Preference methods encourage a model to favor chosen responses over rejected ones, usually with mechanisms intended to prevent excessive optimization. This paper studies a ReLU-based objective without sigmoid-based gradient constraints or explicit regularization terms.

The experiments show that these omissions do not prevent meaningful alignment, but over-optimization remains a real concern. A threshold parameter, gamma, plays an essential role by dynamically filtering training examples. The result therefore points to the importance of controlling which examples continue to influence learning, rather than demonstrating that unrestricted preference optimization is harmless.

The theoretical analysis connects RePO to the convex envelope of the zero-one loss, providing a formal foundation for the objective. Empirically, it achieves competitive or better results than established preference optimization approaches. The contribution is a simple baseline that helps isolate which mechanisms matter: successful learning can occur without the two omitted components, while threshold-based example filtering remains central to the reported behavior.
neurips-2025-repo-understanding-preferen.tldr: RePO achieves competitive preference learning with a simple ReLU objective whose threshold filters examples to help prevent over-optimization.

paragraphs: Reward-oriented causal representation learning asks how much hidden causal structure must be recovered to optimize a particular task. Conventional formulations often pursue complete recovery of latent variables and their causal relationships. This paper instead targets the coarsest representation sufficient for choosing the intervention that optimizes the desired reward.

The formal setting optimizes a function of observable data over possible interventions and focuses on linear causal and transformation models. An adaptive exploration algorithm progressively learns the causal graph and the latent variables needed to identify the best intervention. Its learning objective is therefore tied to decision quality, allowing the task to determine which aspects of the hidden representation matter.

The paper provides an upper regret bound involving observation dimension, latent dimension, graph-estimation uncertainty, and the decision horizon. It also establishes an almost-matching lower bound involving the number of causal paths. These bounds characterize the difficulty of learning useful interventions under the stated model assumptions. They support studying task-sufficient causal knowledge as a distinct objective from perfect recovery of the entire hidden system.
neurips-2025-reward-oriented-causal-repr.tldr: Reward-oriented causal learning recovers only the hidden structure needed to choose good interventions, with regret guarantees for linear models.

paragraphs: This paper explores language models that spend additional computation by repeatedly updating internal representations. A recurrent block can be applied multiple times at inference, giving the model a variable effective depth. Extra reasoning effort therefore occurs in latent space, without requiring the model to express every intermediate step as additional text.

The architecture can operate with small context windows and does not require specialized reasoning training data. The authors also argue that internal reasoning can capture processes that are difficult to express in words. To test the idea, they train a proof-of-concept model from scratch with 3.5 billion parameters on 800 billion tokens.

The model uses varying computation levels and improves significantly with additional compute, especially on mathematics and coding tasks. The architecture also supports zero-shot adjustment of computation per token, key-value cache sharing, and speculative decoding to reduce costs. These findings demonstrate an alternative mechanism for scaling inference effort: increasing repeated internal processing can improve reasoning performance in the tested model, while allowing computation to vary across predictions.
neurips-2025-scaling-up-test-time-comput.tldr: A recurrent language model improves reasoning by spending more inference computation on internal representations through repeated applications of a shared block.

paragraphs: This paper explains self-supervised contrastive learning through its relationship to a supervised objective. The proposed comparison objective excludes contrasts between examples from the same semantic class. The authors prove that standard contrastive learning approximates this negatives-only supervised loss, with a gap that vanishes as the number of semantic classes increases under a label-agnostic, architecture-independent bound.

The analysis also characterizes global minimizers of the supervised objective. Augmentations and examples within a class collapse to shared representations, while class centers form a highly symmetric simplex arrangement. These are properties of the analyzed optima, providing a geometric account of the representation structure favored by that objective.

A further bound studies classification with a linear probe and few labeled examples. Variation along directions between class centers dominates the bound, while the influence of within-class dispersion decreases as more labels become available. Experiments support the predicted relationship between losses, including inverse-class-count decay of their gap, and show that the probing bound closely estimates performance. Together, the results connect unlabeled contrastive training to class-aware geometry and label recovery.
neurips-2025-self-supervised-contrastive.tldr: The paper shows how self-supervised contrastive learning approximates a supervised objective and links its representation geometry to few-shot classification.

paragraphs: Decision-making under partial observability requires actions that both pursue rewards and reveal useful information. An action with limited immediate benefit may help an agent make better decisions later by reducing uncertainty. This paper develops a policy-optimization framework for continuous partially observable Markov decision processes that explicitly accounts for this information-gathering role.

The method expresses policy learning as probabilistic inference in a non-Markovian Feynman–Kac model. In this formulation, decision quality depends on history, and the model anticipates future observations when valuing trajectories. The authors state that this captures the value of gathering information without requiring handcrafted exploration heuristics or suboptimal approximations to that aspect of the problem.

To optimize the policy, the paper introduces a nested sequential Monte Carlo algorithm. It efficiently estimates a history-dependent policy gradient using samples from the optimal trajectory distribution induced by the problem. Evaluations on standard continuous partially observable benchmarks demonstrate effectiveness where existing methods struggle with uncertainty. The contribution connects a representation of information-sensitive decisions with a sampling procedure for learning policies from it.
neurips-2025-sequential-monte-carlo-for-.tldr: A probabilistic policy-learning framework uses nested sequential Monte Carlo to account for the future value of information in partially observed environments.

paragraphs: SmokeViz provides a large collection of satellite smoke-plume examples for wildfire-related machine learning. Its source annotations come from NOAA smoke analysts, whose markings describe smoke presence with coarse spatial and temporal precision. The challenge is to connect those expert annotations to satellite inputs that best represent what the analysts identified.

The paper introduces pseudo-label dimension reduction to improve that alignment. The method retains the original labels while deriving intermediate pseudo-labels that associate each annotation with more representative input data. For SmokeViz, a parent model identifies the single satellite image within an annotation's time window that most closely corresponds to the plume.

This refinement yields a dataset containing more than 160,000 manual annotations. The contribution concerns the quality of the pairing between labels and observations, rather than simply adding more automatically labeled examples. The authors present the refinement method as generalizable to datasets with mismatched spatial or temporal resolutions. SmokeViz is publicly available and is intended to support further research on smoke detection, segmentation, and wildfire-related impacts.
neurips-2025-smokeviz-a-large-scale-sate.tldr: SmokeViz aligns expert smoke annotations with representative satellite images, producing a public dataset with more than 160,000 manual annotations.

paragraphs: Training-Free Bayesianization converts an already trained low-rank language-model adapter into a Bayesian adapter for uncertainty estimation. Existing Bayesian approaches using low-rank weight updates can require complex additional training procedures. This paper instead starts from the learned adapter and searches for an appropriate distribution over its weights without further training.

The search seeks the largest acceptable posterior variance within a restricted family of low-rank isotropic Gaussian distributions. That family specifies the form uncertainty can take, while the search determines its acceptable magnitude. The method thus adds uncertainty around trained weights through variance selection, avoiding a new Bayesian fine-tuning procedure.

The theoretical result is conditional: under mild conditions, this search is equivalent to KL-regularized variational optimization, a generalized form of variational inference. Experiments report better uncertainty estimation and generalization than existing methods. Together, the analysis and results support a comparatively simple route to Bayesian adapters, while keeping the scope clear: the method operates on trained low-rank adapters and searches within the stated posterior family.
neurips-2025-training-free-bayesianizati.tldr: TFB adds Bayesian uncertainty to trained low-rank adapters by searching posterior variance without additional training.

paragraphs: TSPIN improves self-play fine-tuning for language models when expert-written examples are scarce. In the existing SPIN approach, the model repeatedly generates responses and learns from the advantage of annotated responses over those outputs. As this current advantage shrinks, optimization can become unstable. Using a reference policy also creates a discrepancy between the training reward and generation metric.

The proposed method adds a historical comparison against responses generated by the initial policy. Training therefore considers annotated responses, current generated responses, and initial generated responses. Historical advantages can continue to provide a useful learning signal when current advantages diminish. TSPIN also introduces an entropy constraint, with theoretical justification for reference-free fine-tuning that removes the identified training-generation discrepancy.

Across the evaluated tasks, TSPIN outperforms SPIN and progresses more stably over successive iterations. It also matches or exceeds supervised fine-tuning performance using only 25% of the samples in the reported comparisons. The findings support preserving historical learning signals and changing the training constraint as complementary ways to make self-play more useful with limited annotations.
neurips-2025-triplets-better-than-pairs-.tldr: TSPIN stabilizes language-model self-play with historical response comparisons and entropy-constrained, reference-free training, improving performance with scarce annotations.

paragraphs: UltraLED reconstructs scenes containing extremely bright and dark regions from a single short-exposure RAW image. Combining short and long exposures can preserve both ends of the brightness range, but moving content can cause misalignment and ghosting. The paper observes that short exposures already retain useful highlight detail, making recovery of dark regions the main challenge.

The method uses RAW data because its higher bit depth and more predictable noise offer greater potential for this recovery. Its first stage corrects exposure through a ratio map that balances the dynamic range. A second, brightness-aware RAW denoiser then targets detail recovery in dark regions. Relying on one short exposure avoids the need to align separate input frames.

The authors also develop a nine-stop exposure-bracketing pipeline to synthesize realistic ultra-high-dynamic-range images and construct a dataset spanning diverse scenes. Reconstruction uses only the shortest exposure as input. Experiments show significant improvements over existing single-frame approaches, supporting the combination of exposure correction and brightness-aware denoising for recovering detail from this constrained input.
neurips-2025-ultraled-learning-to-see-ev.tldr: UltraLED recovers bright and dark scene detail from one short-exposure RAW image using exposure correction followed by brightness-aware denoising.

paragraphs: TEMPLATE helps select a pretrained time-series model for a downstream task. As the available model pool grows, choosing an appropriate starting point becomes a problem in its own right. The paper develops transferability metrics tailored to temporal data, addressing a gap left by the stronger existing focus on computer-vision model selection.

The framework combines three complementary assessments. Dependency Learning Score measures how well a model captures relationships over time. Pattern Learning Score evaluates whether its representations extract discriminative temporal patterns. Task Adaptation Score assesses generalization across tasks. Together, these scores account for temporal structure, representation usefulness, and adaptability, with support for both classification and regression.

Across five downstream tasks, TEMPLATE more effectively identifies the best pretrained models from heterogeneous candidate pools. Compared with ETran, the reported improvement in weighted Kendall's tau is 35% across those tasks. That statistic concerns the quality of model rankings, so the result supports TEMPLATE as a model-selection tool rather than claiming a 35% improvement in downstream prediction accuracy.
neurips-2025-unified-transferability-met.tldr: TEMPLATE combines temporal-dependency, pattern-quality, and task-adaptation scores to better rank pretrained time-series models for transfer learning.
